source_snapshot.procedure: Run `ethtool -S <device name>` to inspect TX, RX and physical error counts.
source_snapshot.criteria: No error is shown in the terminal, with generic result/photo and unexpected-log collection.

disposition_reason: `ethtool -S` is driver-defined: a relevant CRC or physical error may appear far beyond the first 40 lines, and raw values may be cumulative since driver load. `ip -s link` aggregates a different layer and ping adds only small bidirectional IP traffic. Thus neither substitutes for complete device statistics. A valid result needs the exact interface/port identity, full before/after counter schema and a decision whether the source intends passive health or a traffic stimulus; same-code HMC row154 cannot supply any of those semantics. test_case.test_name: NIC TX/RX check under OS — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Verify that the intended OS NIC interface exposes expected TX/RX activity and does not accumulate disallowed driver or physical-layer error counters during the defined observation or traffic window.
required_package: SUT and NIC PN/serial/BDF/netdev/physical port, driver/firmware and link/peer mapping
Supported ethtool/iproute2 versions and pinned reviewed internal Script revision
Driver-specific counter dictionary identifying TX/RX, drop, CRC, FCS, symbol, alignment and physical errors
Baseline/window and allowed absolute/delta thresholds including treatment of cumulative historical counts
Decision whether source coverage is read-only counter health or requires active TX/RX traffic
If active: isolated peer/interface, address/protocol/frame-size/rate/duration/direction and network-impact limits
test_case.test_command: Identify the exact interface, NIC PN/serial/BDF/port, driver/firmware, link and peer; approve/install ethtool/iproute2; capture complete `ethtool -S <interface>` plus `ip -s link` at baseline; observe the approved window or generate bounded isolated traffic only if engineering retains active TX/RX coverage; capture the same full counters afterward; normalize driver-specific TX/RX/error/drop/CRC/physical fields and deltas, correlate kernel/driver logs and preserve all output without reset or truncation.
test_case.expected_result: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test. Criteria: 1. System should show No error in the terminal."

safety_gate: Do not assume eth0; prove netdev-to-NIC/port/peer identity before collection or traffic
Capture full ethtool statistics and exit status; do not head/tail away counters
Do not clear counters, reset/reconfigure the NIC, change link settings or restart the driver to obtain a clean result
Use secure credentials and verified host identity
Generate traffic only on the approved isolated path and stop on loss, link flap, congestion impact or rising severe errors
Preserve preexisting counters and report absolute values plus deltas; no automatic repair or retry
expected_evidence: ethtool/iproute2 versions and approved internal Script revision
Complete timestamped baseline and post-window `ethtool -S` plus `ip -s link` outputs/exits
Counter dictionary and absolute/delta matrix for TX/RX/drop/CRC/FCS/symbol/alignment/physical fields
Approved active traffic parameters/results if required, including per-direction packet/byte/loss evidence
Relevant kernel/driver logs, anomalies/escalation and engineer verdict
